 LIHEAP fall subsidy to help eligible households with heating costs
 By Phoenix Stevens 
 October 29, 2026 | 12:12 am
 Updated October 29, 2026 | 1:09 am
 Share Tweet Print 
 Audubon Area Community Services will begin accepting applications for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) fall subsidy on Nov. 9, offering eligible households help with heating costs.
 Applications will be accepted through Dec. 18 on a first-come, first-served basis or until available funding runs out. The program provides a one-time benefit to help offset home heating expenses, with payments made directly to the household’s energy vendor.
 To qualify, households must have an income at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. Monthly income limits include $1,995 for a one-person household, $2,693 for two people, $3,391 for three people, and $4,125 for four people.
 Applicants do not need a past-due bill, disconnection notice, or eviction notice to receive assistance. Assistance received during previous LIHEAP seasons does not affect eligibility.
 Residents can apply by contacting Audubon Area Community Services offices in Daviess, Hancock, Henderson, McLean, Ohio, Union, and Webster counties.
 Applicants should bring:
 Proof of a Social Security number or Permanent Resident Card (Green Card) for each household member.
 Proof of income for all household members from the previous month.
 The most recent electric bill, a statement from the landlord if heating costs are included in rent, or documentation from the utility company if enrolled in a pre-pay electric program.
 The account number and account holder’s name for the household’s main heating fuel source and electric service.
 More information, including additional income limits and county office locations, is available through Audubon Area Community Services .
